q: Sec. 2.1.1 through 2.1.5 names five phases for Design-Build Services by Administration. Which one below is not among them?
n: The five listed phases are Project Definition, Schematic Design, Design Development, Contract Document, and Construction Phase — there is no separate Post-Construction Phase under this scope. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1.1-2.1.5)

q: Given the figures above, Sec. 2.2.3's guaranteed maximum construction cost ceiling — the estimate plus the 10% allowance — comes out to how much?
n: PHP 10,000,000 estimated cost + 10% (PHP 1,000,000) = PHP 11,000,000, the ceiling beyond which Sec. 2.2.3 makes the Architect liable for the excess. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.3)
scenario: Under Design-Build Services structured around a Guaranteed Maximum Project Construction Cost, an Architect quotes the Owner/Client an estimated project construction cost of PHP 10,000,000, while his Administration Fee for the project is set at PHP 500,000.

q: The last of the expanded Construction Phase duties in Sec. 2.1.5(h) covers management of what?
o: All other business tied to construction
n: Item (h) covers management of all other business transactions related to the project construction/implementation, as a catch-all duty. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1.5(h))

q: With the Owner/Client's approval, Sec. 4.3 allows the Architect to bring on which support staff beyond the usual labor force?
o: An independent financial auditor and a government building official
A Professional Advisor and a Competition Secretariat
A separate licensed Architect of record and a design competition Jury
A construction superintendent, purchasing agent, timekeeper, and property clerk
n: Sec. 4.3 lists a construction superintendent, purchasing agent, timekeeper and property clerk as personnel the Architect may appoint, subject to Owner/Client approval. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 4.3)

q: Sec. 2.1.5(g) has the Architect negotiate with which parties concerning jurisdiction over the project?
o: Government and private agencies having jurisdiction over the project
Competing Architects bidding for the same project
n: Item (g) lists negotiation with Government and private agencies having jurisdiction over the project. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1.5(g))

q: Sec. 1.2 says the various project-delivery methods devised by the building industry and the profession all aim at what common goal?
o: Shortest time, lowest cost, acceptable quality
Shifting all risk to the Owner
n: Sec. 1.2 describes the goal as handling projects in the shortest possible time, at the lowest possible cost, and at an acceptable quality and performance. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 1.2)

q: No matter which Sec. 3.1 arrangement he takes on, what does Sec. 3.2.1 require the Architect to hold onto without fail?
o: The right to waive professional liability for construction defects
A distinct corporate entity registered with the SEC
His separate and distinct professional identity, prerogatives, and integrity as an Architect
Exclusive control over the Owner/Client's financing arrangements
n: Sec. 3.2.1 requires the Architect to retain his separate/distinct professional identity, prerogatives and integrity as an Architect. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 3.2.1)

q: If an Architect wants a hand in construction (even of his own design) outside the usual bidding process or Design-Build modes, what does Sec. 3.1 let him do?
o: Forfeit his design fee to the contractor
Hand supervision to a third party
Only form a joint venture with the Client
Join the builder, or act as a licensed contractor
n: Sec. 3.1.1 allows the Architect to be part of or a member of the entity constructing his design, and Sec. 3.1.2 allows him to be himself a State-licensed contractor implementing his design (or that of others). (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 3.1.1-3.1.2)

q: Sec. 1.4 says Design-Build Services streamlines and speeds up project delivery while offering what type of solutions?
o: Solutions confined strictly to residential projects
n: Sec. 1.4 states that Design-Build Services simplifies and expedites project delivery while providing creative cost-effective solutions. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 1.4)

q: Building on the same figures, say the final construction cost lands at PHP 11,300,000 — PHP 300,000 over the PHP 11,000,000 guaranteed maximum — with no legitimate CVOs/EWOs or certified escalation behind it. Under Sec. 2.2.3, how much of that overage falls on the Architect?
o: The full PHP 1,300,000 actual cost above the original estimate
PHP 300,000, since that amount is less than his PHP 500,000 Administration Fee
The Owner/Client automatically absorbs the entire overage
A flat PHP 500,000, no matter the actual excess
n: Sec. 2.2.3 makes the Architect liable for the excess amount over the guaranteed maximum, but only up to the amount of his Administration Fee. Here the excess (PHP 300,000) is less than the PHP 500,000 fee, so the Architect is liable for the full PHP 300,000 excess. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.3)
scenario: Under Design-Build Services structured around a Guaranteed Maximum Project Construction Cost, an Architect quotes the Owner/Client an estimated project construction cost of PHP 10,000,000, while his Administration Fee for the project is set at PHP 500,000.

q: When spending beyond the guaranteed maximum construction cost stems from legitimate CVOs, EWOs, or certified substantial cost escalation, Sec. 2.2.4 puts the burden on whom?
o: The Architect's professional liability insurer, automatically
The Architect, deducted from his Administration Fee
n: Sec. 2.2.4 provides that such additional costs, being due to causes not attributable to the Architect's fault, shall be borne by the Owner/Client. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.4)

q: Say an Architect handling Design-Build Services has a personal stake in a project supplier, raising a conflict-of-interest concern. What does the Architects Credo cited in Sec. 3.2.2 commit him to do?
o: Pass its profits to the Client
n: Sec. 3.2.2 quotes the Architects Credo pledge to disclose whenever required any business investment or venture that may create a conflict of interest, ensuring it neither compromises the Client's legitimate interest nor interferes with the duty to render impartial judgment. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 3.2.2 / Architects Credo)

q: Among the Architect's expanded Construction Phase duties under Design-Build Services by Administration, which of these is included?
o: Organizing and hiring construction personnel, and assigning their duties and pay
Approving his own guaranteed maximum cost estimate
Issuing the Certificate of Occupancy on the building official's behalf
Serving as Professional Advisor to a design competition Jury
n: Item (b) of Sec. 2.1.5 lists organization and hiring of construction personnel, and designation of duties and remunerations, as an expanded Construction Phase duty. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1.5(b))

q: Sec. 2.1 likens the scope of Design-Build Services by Administration to the Regular Design Services scope in which SPP Document?
n: Sec. 2.1 states the scope of Design-Build Services by Administration is similar to that of the Architect's Regular Design Services under SPP Document 202. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1)

q: Sec. 4.1 ties the Architect's payment schedule under Design-Build Services to what?
o: Completion of the whole project, paid in one lump sum
The Architect's original design-fee schedule alone
A fixed monthly retainer, irrespective of progress
n: Sec. 4.1 states the manner of payment to the Architect follows the progress of construction. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 4.1)

q: Still using those figures, imagine the project instead ends up costing PHP 12,500,000 — PHP 1,500,000 over the PHP 11,000,000 guaranteed maximum — again with no legitimate CVOs/EWOs or certified escalation. How much of that must the Architect shoulder under Sec. 2.2.3?
o: PHP 1,000,000, equal to 10% of the estimated cost
Nothing, since the overage is beyond his control
PHP 500,000 — the ceiling set by his Administration Fee
n: Sec. 2.2.3 caps the Architect's liability for the excess at the amount of his Administration Fee. Even though the actual excess is PHP 1,500,000, the Architect is liable only up to his PHP 500,000 Administration Fee. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.3)
scenario: Under Design-Build Services structured around a Guaranteed Maximum Project Construction Cost, an Architect quotes the Owner/Client an estimated project construction cost of PHP 10,000,000, while his Administration Fee for the project is set at PHP 500,000.

q: When an Architect, being himself a State-licensed contractor, personally carries out a design (his own or someone else's), which SPP Document 207 provision applies?
n: Sec. 3.1.2 specifically covers the Architect being himself a State-licensed contractor implementing his design or that of others. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 3.1.2)

q: Who covers the salaries of the construction superintendent, purchasing agent, timekeeper, and property clerk under Sec. 4.3, and can these be deducted from the Architect's Fee?
o: Paid by the Owner/Client, but deducted from the Architect's Fee at year-end
Paid by the Owner/Client, and not deductible from the Architect's Fee
Split evenly between the Architect and the Owner/Client
Paid by the Architect, and fully deductible from his Fee
n: Sec. 4.3 states these salaries are paid by the Owner/Client and are not deductible from the Architect's Fee under this SPP. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 4.3)

q: Under Sec. 4.2, who bears the cost of all permits, licenses, and other incidentals to the work?
n: Sec. 4.2 states the Owner/Client shall pay for the cost of all permits, licenses and other incidentals to the work. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 4.2)

q: According to Sec. 4.1, who pays labor and material costs directly, with the Architect never fronting money for these expenses?
n: Sec. 4.1 states the Client directly pays all costs for labor and materials, and the Architect does not advance any money for payment of related expenditures. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 4.1)

q: What liability trait, per Sec. 1.5, sets Design-Build Services apart from the Architect's regular design services?
o: Liability for both design and construction
Liability shared equally with the contractor
n: Sec. 1.5 provides that in Design-Build Services the Architect assumes professional responsibility and civil liability for both the design and the construction of the project. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 1.5)

q: Per Sec. 2.2.3, the Architect guarantees the actual construction cost won't exceed the estimate by more than what percentage?
n: Sec. 2.2.3 states the project construction cost is guaranteed by the Architect not to exceed Ten Percent (10%) of the estimated project construction cost. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.3)
scenario: Under Design-Build Services structured around a Guaranteed Maximum Project Construction Cost, an Architect quotes the Owner/Client an estimated project construction cost of PHP 10,000,000, while his Administration Fee for the project is set at PHP 500,000.

q: With the same figures, the project ultimately wraps up at PHP 9,200,000. Under Sec. 2.2.2, what share of the resulting savings goes to the Architect?
o: PHP 0 — the savings belong entirely to the Owner
n: The savings is PHP 10,000,000 − PHP 9,200,000 = PHP 800,000. Sec. 2.2.2 divides this equally between Owner/Client and Architect, giving the Architect PHP 400,000. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.2)
scenario: Under Design-Build Services structured around a Guaranteed Maximum Project Construction Cost, an Architect quotes the Owner/Client an estimated project construction cost of PHP 10,000,000, while his Administration Fee for the project is set at PHP 500,000.

q: Which older document did SPP Document 207 (on Design-Build Services) replace?
n: The header of SPP Document 207 states it replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 207. (Source: SPP Document 207, title page note)

q: Whatever construction-involvement arrangement he adopts, Sec. 3.2.1 keeps the Architect bound by the SPP's standards — specifically which two documents?
n: Sec. 3.2.1 names SPP Document 200, the Code of Ethical Conduct, and SPP Document 202 as the standards the Architect remains subject to. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 3.2.1)

q: When a Guaranteed Maximum Cost project finishes under its estimated construction cost, what happens to the resulting savings?
o: It goes entirely to the Architect
It is split evenly between the Owner/Client and the Architect
The general contractor forfeits any claim to it
It goes entirely to the Owner/Client
n: Sec. 2.2.2 provides that if there is realized savings from the estimated project construction cost, it is divided equally between the Owner/Client and the Architect. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.2)
scenario: Under Design-Build Services structured around a Guaranteed Maximum Project Construction Cost, an Architect quotes the Owner/Client an estimated project construction cost of PHP 10,000,000, while his Administration Fee for the project is set at PHP 500,000.

q: What sets Design-Build Services under a Guaranteed Maximum Project Construction Cost (Sec. 2.2) apart from Design-Build Services by Administration (Sec. 2.1)?
o: The Owner/Client is barred from sharing in any cost savings
The five design phases from Sec. 2.1 are done away with entirely
The Architect gives the Owner/Client a guaranteed maximum project construction cost
The Architect stops performing any design services whatsoever
n: Sec. 2.2.1 states this method is essentially the same as Design-Build Services by Administration, except the Architect provides a guaranteed maximum project construction cost. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.1)

q: During the expanded Construction Phase, Sec. 2.1.5(d) has the Architect procuring what?
o: Entries for a design competition, for jury review
Only office supplies for the site office
Insurance policies covering the Owner/Client's other properties
Materials, plants and equipment, and licenses and permits
n: Item (d) lists procurement of materials, plants and equipment, licenses and permits. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1.5(d))

q: Under Design-Build Services by Administration, at what point do the Architect's Construction Phase duties extend past mere periodic inspection and assessment?
o: Once the various design-service phases have been completed
Never — periodic inspection remains the outer limit
Only if the Owner/Client requests it in writing
Only for projects above a certain floor area
n: Sec. 2.1.5 states that once the various phases of design services are completed, the Construction Phase goes beyond periodic inspection and assessment to include additional duties (items a-h). (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1.5)

q: Sec. 4.1 has what kind of fund typically advanced to the Architect beforehand, to be accounted for and periodically audited by the Client?
n: Sec. 4.1 provides that a revolving fund is generally given to the Architect beforehand, accounted for and subject to periodic auditing by the Client. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 4.1)

q: When an Architect negotiates and signs a contract with a piecework contractor, then evaluates that contractor's work output, which expanded Construction Phase duty is this?
o: Item (h) — managing all other business transactions related to the project
Item (g) — negotiating with government and private agencies having jurisdiction over the project
Item (c) — negotiating and contracting with piecework contractors, and evaluating their work accomplishments
Item (a) — preparing the schedule of work and estimates of materials, labor, transportation, equipment, and services
n: Item (c) specifically covers negotiating and entering into contracts with piecework contractors and evaluating work accomplishments. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1.5(c))

q: Sec. 4.4 permits modifying the Design-Build compensation method using alternatives spelled out in which SPP Document?
n: Sec. 4.4 states the method of compensation may be modified by using the relevant alternatives detailed in SPP Doc. 202. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 4.4)

q: Among the expanded Construction Phase duties, Sec. 2.1.5(f) makes the Architect responsible for keeping what?
o: Minutes of the design-competition Jury's deliberations
n: Item (f) lists keeping records and books of accounts as an expanded Construction Phase duty. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.1.5(f))

q: Sec. 2.2.4 names which nationally recognized agency as an example of a body that can certify substantial escalation in material or labor costs?
o: The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture (PRBoA)
The Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA)
The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI)
n: Sec. 2.2.4 cites the National Economic Development Authority (NEDA) as an example of a nationally recognized agency that may certify such data. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.4)

q: Sec. 1.3 attributes an Architect's ability to take a direct hand in a project from conception through implementation to what?
o: A special contractor's license issued by the IAPOA
His seniority relative to other architects on the project
His membership on the jury of design competitions
n: Sec. 1.3 attributes this qualification to the Architect's education, training and expertise. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 1.3)

q: What do the abbreviations "CVOs" and "EWOs" stand for, per Sec. 2.2.4?
o: Cost variance offsets and emergency work orders
Contractor verification orders and equipment withdrawal orders
Certified valuation orders and estimated work outlays
Change/variation orders and extra work orders
n: Sec. 2.2.4 uses CVOs to mean change/variation orders and EWOs to mean extra work orders. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 2.2.4)

q: Sec. 1.1 names three elements a building project must balance, which Design-Build Services is well-suited to deliver. What are they?
n: Sec. 1.1 states the need to balance time, quality and cost, which in many cases is best achieved through Design-Build Services. (Source: SPP Document 207, Sec. 1.1)
